OPENCODE / LOCAL MODELS

OpenCode with Ollama: local models, 64K context and troubleshooting

With Ollama and OpenCode installed, start with ollama launch opencode and choose a local model. After a request, use ollama ps to check the model, allocated context and CPU/GPU split. Local chat is only the first check; a coding agent also needs sufficient context and working tool calls.

Published：2026-11-23 · OpenCode V2

  1. Launch OpenCode and select a local model
  2. Empty model list: check the server and discovery
  3. Insufficient context, slow responses or memory pressure
  4. Chat works but code edits fail: check tool calls
  5. Verify the local request before using a real project

Where does the local setup stop working?

Launch OpenCode and select a local model

Install and start Ollama and OpenCode, then run this in a disposable project without private files:

ollama launch opencode

Confirm the picker selects a local model. Cloud models send inference requests to a remote service. A first download needs network access, disk space and time; no single model fits every memory budget. If launch is unavailable, check ollama --version against the official installation guidance.

Use ollama launch opencode --config for configuration without an interactive session. Back up existing project settings before merging changes. A successful launch is not yet proof that a local request completed.

Empty model list: check the server and discovery

From the machine running the OpenCode server, inspect Ollama’s native inventory:

curl --fail --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags

The response should contain a models list. An empty list means no models are listed by that server; a refused connection needs a server or address check first. Return to /models after installing a model. V2 discovers local Ollama without account setup; embedding-only models are excluded.

Inside a container or on another computer, loopback points to that environment itself. For a remote server, use a reachable address and establish access controls before opening its port. Native V2 endpoint example:

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "providers": {
    "ollama": {
      "settings": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1" }
    }
  }
}

This uses the V2 providers/settings shape. Do not mix it with older provider/options fields inside the same provider entry. Select an actual model ID from your local /models list.

Insufficient context, slow responses or memory pressure

Ollama’s OpenCode integration requires at least 64K context. Larger context consumes more memory, so check model support and available memory first. Adjust the Ollama app setting, or stop an existing manually managed service before starting:

OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 ollama serve

A second server cannot use an already occupied port. After sending a request, run:

ollama ps

Inspect NAME, CONTEXT and PROCESSOR. If context is smaller than intended, check whether the running service received the new setting. For CPU offloading or memory pressure, evaluate a smaller model that can accommodate the required context. A larger client-side limit does not allocate server memory or extend the model’s actual limit.

For hardware tradeoffs, see our Mac mini 32GB Qwen measurements (Chinese). Those observations use MLX backends, not this Ollama setup or a 64K agent task; their speeds do not transfer directly.

Chat works but code edits fail: check tool calls

In a disposable repository, request an explanation of a small file, then permit one bounded edit. Inspect the actual tool call, permission request, diff and test result. Printed tool JSON or a claim that a file changed is not a completed edit.

Verify model and server tool support before investigating context and permissions. Granting unrestricted access does not fix unsupported tool calling. For unavailable models, authentication errors or timeouts, use the OpenCode connection troubleshooting guide.

Verify the local request before using a real project

Match the selected provider/model and endpoint with the running model in ollama ps and the corresponding server log. A running process alone does not identify which server answered a request. Local inference also leaves web access, MCP servers, plugins and other model connections to check separately.

Save a minimal request, allocated context, memory state and task result before expanding the trial. Record both versions and redacted configuration if it fails. This is a documentation-based setup guide; we have not performed a new installation, inference benchmark or complete coding task for it.
